USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client Star Steel Structures & Frames Pty Ltd (SSSF), ABN: 52 630 055 248 located at: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760 is a Premier Steel supply and installation company. It is a 100% Australian owned company that provides customisable solutions in high-quality reinforcing mesh, structural steel, and prefabrication services, specializing in eco-friendly construction materials. They focus on delivering durable, moisture-resistant, and heat-resistant products made from 100% recyclable steel. With a commitment to sustainability, Star steel ensures a 48-hour turnaround for quotes while adhering to Australian construction standards. Their products are designed for maximum efficiency and reliability, serving the needs of construction professionals who value quality and eco-conscious solutions.

Due to the business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit Welder(s) in their Operations team on a permanent full-time basis. We are seeking an experienced Welder or maybe two, to join our operations team on a full-time basis. The successful candidate will be responsible for fabricating, joining, and repairing metal components and structures using a range of welding techniques, working from technical drawings and specifications to produce high-quality, structurally sound welds in accordance with the relevant Australian standards.

Position: Welder
No of positions: 02
Reports to: Operations Head / Supervisor
Location: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760
Annual salary range: AUD $80,000 - $85,000 base + Super (for a 38-hour work week)

As a Welder, your main duties and responsibilities includes:
•	Ensuring all work is carried out in compliance with WHS regulations and relevant Australian Standards.
•	Cutting, bending, shaping, joining and repairing metal components of iron and steel structures, boilers, pressure vessels and pipes.
•	Studying blueprints, drawings and specifications to determine job requirements.
•	Selecting, cleaning and preparing metal stock.
•	Cutting marked-out metal sections and shapes using hand tools, flame cutting torches and metal cutting machines.
•	Shaping and bending metal sections and pipes using hand and machine tools and by heating and hammering.
•	Aligning parts to be joined using hand tools and measuring instruments.
•	Joining metal sections using various welding techniques, bolting and riveting.
•	Examining welds for width of bead, penetration and precision.
•	Finishing products by cleaning, polishing, filing and bathing in acidic solutions. 
•	Cleaning and smoothing welds by filing, chiselling and grinding.
•	Selecting and applying appropriate welding processes (manual metal arc, gas metal arc, advanced welding techniques) based on material and job specifications.
•	 Assembling fabricated components in line with technical drawings.
•	Applying safe welding practices and maintaining accurate weld records.
•	Operating fixed and mobile load-shifting equipment at workshop as required.
•	Working safely and effectively within manufacturing and engineering environments, complying with WHS and environmental sustainability requirements. 
•	Performing engineering measurements, inspections and quality checks on completed welds and fabricated items.
•	Ordering materials and planning work activities to meet production schedules.
•	Organising and communicating information with supervisors and team members. 
•	Using hand tools, power tools and computing technology relevant to fabrication and welding tasks.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Engineering - Fabrication Trade – Welder (First class) preferred.
•	At least 5 years of proven work experience in the above job role. 
•	Sound welding experience in manual / advanced metal arc welding & Gas metal arc welding process. 
•	Well experienced of WHS requirements, particularly in manufacturing and steel fabrication environment. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.

Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask and physically fit
•	Process and results driven 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive & hard-working

Additional information: 
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when delivering key orders. 
•	Ability to travel interstate if required

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Help Redesign the Future of Healthcare in Australia

Shape One of Australia's Largest Healthcare Transformations-Join the team delivering Bringing Care Home, St Vincent's bold vision to care for 50% of patients and residents through virtual and in-home settings by 2030. This is an opportunity to influence how healthcare is delivered across Australia for generations to come.

Lead at the Intersection of Cloud, AI and Digital Health-Design and architect a next-generation ecosystem spanning patient and clinician applications, remote patient monitoring, AI-enabled services, cloud-native platforms, and enterprise healthcare integrations.

Build Something New, Not Maintain the Past-This is not a BAU architecture role. You will help establish the technical foundations, standards, and future-state architecture for a nationally significant transformation program from the ground up.

About Bringing Care Home

For more than 160 years, St Vincent's has delivered care where it is needed most.

Today, we're doing it again.

Bringing Care Home is our enterprise-wide transformation to deliver more connected, personalised and accessible healthcare through virtual care, remote patient monitoring, digital health technologies and innovative models of care.

This is more than a technology transformation - it's a transformation of healthcare itself.

The Opportunity- Lead Solutions Architect - Bringing Care Home Transformation 

This is a permanent full-time position with flexible hybrid working arrangements available across Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane.

Reporting initially to the National Director, Architecture & Portfolio Management, and transitioning into the Bringing Care Home leadership structure as the program matures, you will serve as the technical authority responsible for shaping the architecture that underpins one of Australia's most significant healthcare transformation programs.

Working at the intersection of cloud, AI, digital health and virtual care, you will provide architecture leadership across a complex ecosystem of patient and clinician applications, remote patient monitoring platforms, enterprise integrations, healthcare data services and emerging technologies. Partnering closely with executives, clinicians, product teams, architects, engineers and delivery partners, you will ensure technology decisions are scalable, secure, future-focused and aligned to exceptional patient outcomes.

You will lead the design and technical direction of:

Patient and clinician-facing mobile applications

Cloud-native digital healthcare platforms

Remote patient monitoring solutions

Enterprise integration services

AI-enabled healthcare capabilities

Secure healthcare data ecosystems

Modern DevSecOps and delivery practices

Working across executives, clinicians, product teams, engineers, architects, and delivery partners, you will ensure technology decisions support exceptional patient outcomes while remaining scalable, secure, and aligned to enterprise standards.

How You'll Make an Impact

Success in this role will see you:

Establish the architecture foundations that enable scalable virtual and in-home healthcare services nationally

Deliver solution architectures across key digital, cloud, integration, data and AI initiatives

Create reusable design patterns, standards and governance frameworks that accelerate future delivery

Drive alignment across multiple delivery partners, platforms and technology workstreams

Champion modern engineering practices - cloud-native architecture, DevSecOps, automation, and AI-enabled solutions - applying them hands-on, not just as guiding principles

Provide trusted technical leadership to executives, clinicians and technology teams

Contribute to positioning St Vincent's as a leader in digitally enabled healthcare innovation

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership

Provide architecture leadership across a complex multi-partner environment, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable and fit for purpose.

Solution Architecture

Lead end-to-end architecture across applications, cloud, integration, data, AI and clinical technology domains.

Innovation & Modern Engineering

Champion and personally apply cloud-native architectures, automation, AI-enabled capabilities, and contemporary software delivery practices. This includes hands-on involvement in spikes, proof-of-concepts, and design validation - not solely governance and oversight.

Governance & Risk

Provide design assurance, architectural governance and proactive risk management across major initiatives.

Stakeholder Engagement

Translate complex technical concepts into meaningful business outcomes for executives, clinicians, vendors and delivery teams.

About You

You are an experienced Technical Architect with a strong engineering background - you have come up through platform engineering, software engineering, or cloud engineering, and you still get hands-on. You have a proven track record delivering complex digital transformation programs within enterprise environments, and you have been actively building and shipping cloud-native and AI-enabled solutions in the last two years - not just advising on them.

You will bring:

7+ years' experience within large-scale technology environments, including at least 3 years in a Technical or Solution Architect role - and critically, hands-on technical implementation experience in cloud and AI within the last 2 years. Candidates who have moved fully away from hands-on delivery will not be the right fit for this role

Demonstrated, recent hands-on experience (within the last 2 years) designing and delivering enterprise-grade solutions across AWS and-or Azure cloud environments

Mandatory: Deep, hands-on expertise in cloud-native architecture - API-led integration, event-driven platforms, enterprise data architecture, containerised and serverless technologies, and modern DevSecOps and CI-CD practices. You have built and shipped these patterns, not just designed them on whiteboards

Experience designing customer, patient, clinician or employee-facing digital products, including mobile and web-based applications

Proven capability delivering architecture across multiple domains including applications, integration, cloud, data and security

Mandatory: Demonstrated hands-on experience designing and implementing AI-enabled applications using modern AI services (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, LLM APIs, conversational AI, agentic workflows) - you have built with these tools, not just recommended them

An engineering mindset: you are comfortable doing technical spikes, validating integration approaches hands-on, reviewing code and infrastructure, and working alongside engineers to unblock delivery - architecture for you is a doing discipline, not just a thinking one

Ability to provide technical leadership and influence stakeholders across business, clinical, product and technology teams within complex delivery environments

Highly Regarded

result.description:
Position: Telecommunications Technical Officer
Type: Full-time
Employer: Online Star PTY LTD
Location: Canberra ACT
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business
Online Star PTY LTD is a dynamic Canberra-based provider of telecommunications services and solutions, alongside IT services, dedicated to optimising business performance and unlocking new revenue streams in the rapidly evolving communications sector. With a team of highly experienced professionals, we partner with major telecom operators and vendors to deliver customised solutions that help clients enter new markets, defend existing ones, secure networks, improve quality, and deploy infrastructure efficiently. Our core values centre on innovation, operational excellence, cost-effectiveness, and high-quality service delivery, fostering a collaborative and supportive workplace culture where technical expertise drives tangible business outcomes and subscriber satisfaction.
About the Position
The Telecommunications Technical Officer plays a critical role at Online Star PTY LTD in supporting the delivery of NBN fibre and telecommunications network projects. This position involves field-based technical support, testing coordination, quality oversight and technical guidance across active project sites. The role sits between the Project Engineers and the field technicians and is essential to ensuring that network works are delivered to the required technical standards, that faults are diagnosed and rectified efficiently, and that completed works meet client acceptance requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Reviewing job packs, network plans, asset records and scopes of work before field work begins and confirming the design intent against site conditions.
Attending project sites to assess ground conditions, identify service and access risks, and confirm the scoped works can be built to the client design and NBN requirements.
Providing technical direction to field technicians during fibre hauling, splicing, pit and pipe works, exchange patching and BNTD installation.
Coordinating and verifying fibre testing using OTDR and optical power meters, and validating results against applicable NBN and client acceptance requirements before handover to the delivery partner.
Diagnosing fibre, duct, patching and connection faults on site, tracing the cause and setting out the rectification steps required to keep the job on schedule.
Checking completed works against the plans, job packs and NBN specifications, and confirming they are ready for submission to the project manager or delivery partner.
Preparing and updating as-built records, test results, site reports, defect notes and completion packs.
Coordinating with project engineers, supervisors, delivery partners, subcontractors and customers on site access, progress, technical issues and completion sign-off.
Monitoring crews on site to confirm they follow the approved work method, the SWMS and the relevant technical standards.
Escalating complex design, structural or safety matters to the Project Engineers or management where higher-level approval is required.
Reviewing rejected or non-compliant work, identifying why it failed, and instructing field crews on the correct method to bring it back to standard.
Keeping records of materials, equipment, test outcomes, network locations and work status to support project tracking and partner reporting.
Monitoring the performance of completed fibre network segments, interpreting transmission and optical test results, and identifying where network performance requires correction or improvement.
Configuring and integrating telecommunications network equipment, including BNTDs and related network access equipment, and verifying correct operation after installation.
Ensuring compliance with Work Health and Safety obligations on all project sites.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant field.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience.
Strong technical skills in telecommunications network testing, fault diagnosis, equipment configuration and integration, including practical experience with OTDR and optical power meters.
Excellent problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and the capacity to maintain accurate documentation and logs.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills for liaising with internal teams, delivery partners, vendors and clients.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with a focus on quality standards and operational efficiency.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
